Everywhere there were exquisite kalpavṛkṣa trees; everywhere there were pure, magnificent springs and ponds filled with water possessing the eight virtues. All ordinary human beings had been removed, and furthermore, the sound of women was not heard.
In every place, vast lotus flowers appeared; each flower was as large as a chariot wheel, and within each lotus sat a bodhisattva image in the full-lotus posture.
Furthermore, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Amitāyus, was manifest, teaching the Dharma in the company of various bodhisattvas.

He was surrounded by countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Śakras, Brahmās, Lokapālas, and other devas, as well as by a multitude of countless hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of bodhisattvas who gathered to listen to the Dharma; that is to say, he likewise preached this very Dharma-gate.
At that time, having thus manifested herself, the goddess Dīrghāyu arose from samādhi and, after circumambulating the World-Honored One three times to the right, vanished from sight.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!

If there are good sons or good daughters who, regarding this True Dharma, hear it, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, remember it, explain its meaning, and further expound it extensively for others—how much merit will such a person obtain?"
The Buddha said:
"Good son! Suppose the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world were filled with sentient beings, all of whom practiced giving continuously for immeasurable time without interruption."

If there are good sons or good daughters who give rise to a pure mind toward this True Dharma, transcribe it according to the Dharma and carefully proofread it, and furthermore, with a pure mind, bestow it upon others, the merit and virtue obtained by such a person will be many times greater than the former.
Why is this? O son of good family!
Material giving does not lead one out of birth and death, whereas the gift of Dharma is supreme and most excellent.

Why is this? Because all sentient beings within the cycle of birth and death, due to their craving for various forms of wealth and profit, are unable to partake of the flavor of that supreme Dharma to transcend the world.
"Furthermore, noble son!
Suppose there were someone who caused all sentient beings filling this trichiliocosm to dwell securely in the ten paths of wholesome action."

Furthermore, if there should be another person who hears, receives, upholds, recites, memorizes, explains its meaning, and extensively expounds this True Dharma to others, the merit obtained by that person will be many times greater than the former.
Why is this? Good son!
The ten paths of wholesome action are born from this True Dharma.
"Furthermore, son of good family!

Suppose the sentient beings filling the entire trichiliocosm were all to cause them to realize the fruit of stream-entry, the fruit of once-returning, the fruit of non-returning, and the fruit of arhatship."

If, moreover, there should be someone who hears, receives, upholds, reads, recites, remembers, explains the meaning of, and further extensively proclaims this True Dharma to others, the merit obtained by that person will be many times greater than the former.
Why is this? Son of good family!
You should know that all śrāvakas and pratyekabuddhas have likewise emerged from within this very nature of phenomena (dharmatā).
All bodhisattvas likewise come forth from within this very dharma-nature;
it is because the Tathāgata has also realized this dharma-nature that he appears in the world.
Furthermore, son of good family!

If a person can receive, uphold, read, recite, and understand the meaning of such a true Dharma, that person is equivalent to one who receives, upholds, reads, recites, and explains the essential meanings within all the sutras.
Why is this? This nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is the mother of all phenomena.
O son of good family!
"Furthermore, if Bodhisattvas do not attain this nature of the true Dharma, they will be unable to attain the vast nature of the Dharma.
At that time, the great Śrāvakas in the assembly each rose from their seats, bared their right shoulders, knelt with their right knees on the ground, and together addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"Having attained this nature of phenomena (dharmatā), will we be able to bring the vast cycle of birth and death to a complete end?
The Buddha said, "O Bhikṣus!"
"So it is, so it is. At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the entire assembly gathered there, saying:
"O sons of good family!

In whatever region there may be a place where such a sublime Dharma is being proclaimed, that region should be known as the site of great enlightenment, the place where the wheel of Dharma is turned, and the site of a great reliquary stūpa;
one should form this thought: "This is the place where my Great Teacher dwells."
Why is this? Good son! The nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is itself awakening (bodhi), and it is itself the turning of the wheel of Dharma; the wheel of Dharma is itself the Tathāgata.
“Good son! If one makes offerings to the Dharma, this is equivalent to making offerings to all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas.
In whatever region a Dharma teacher dwells, one should regard that place as a sacred stūpa and regard the Dharma teacher as the Great Teacher.”
Furthermore, one should conceive of them as spiritual friends (kalyāṇamitra) and should likewise conceive of them as excellent guides.

For this reason, whenever one sees that Dharma teacher, one should give rise to a heart of pure faith and joy, honoring and revering them by welcoming them before oneself, praising and extolling them, and saying:
"Excellent!"
"Furthermore, son of good family!

If I were to praise and speak of the merit of honoring and revering the Dharma teacher, as well as speaking of repaying the great kindness of that Dharma teacher—such matters as these, even if I were to spend an eon or more than an eon, I could not describe even a small fraction of them."

“Good son! If there are good sons and good daughters who love and delight in the Dharma, even if they were to sprinkle their own blood upon the ground along the path where a Dharma teacher walks, they still could not repay even a small fraction of that Dharma teacher’s debt of gratitude.”
Why is this? Because a Dharma-preacher is able to uphold the Tathāgata’s Dharma-eye, which is an extremely difficult practice to perform.
"Good son!..."

Therefore, when all Dharma-preachers speak such true Dharma, they should manifest fearlessness; they should not become dejected or give rise to obstructive thoughts, but should put on fresh, clean robes and arouse a pure mind.

When the Dharma is being taught, if one does not give rise to arrogance upon receiving praise, does not manifest the mark of a self, does not produce conceit or attachment, does not extol oneself nor disparage others, and furthermore does not give rise to a mind of defiled clinging, one should instead revere and respect the teaching of the Dharma.
At that time, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, came forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

In whatever regions there may be places where such a True Dharma is being taught, I shall lead my retinue of palace attendants to those locations to listen to and receive this most profound True Dharma, and to provide protection and assistance to those teachers of the Dharma.”
The Buddha said:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
“Kauśika! You have well guarded the True Dharma of the Tathāgata; what you have done is precisely what is required at this very time.
At that moment, the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
What is the name of this sutra?
How should we receive and uphold it?”
The Buddha said, “Good son!

This sutra is titled ‘The Questions of Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin,’ and it is also titled ‘Jewel Cloud’ (Ratnamegha), and also titled ‘Accumulation of Jewel Merit,’ and also titled ‘Lamp of Wisdom. You should receive and uphold these names.”

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas such as Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, the entire assembly of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as well as the assembly of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas present there, Śakra, Brahmā, the World-Protectors, the gods, Maheśvara, the sons of heaven, and countless hundreds of thousands of devaputras, along with other countless hundreds of thousands of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and the entire great assembly, having heard what the Buddha taught, rejoiced and accepted it with faith.
